$comment: Curated patch-generation benchmark. Cases are identified by their gap identity
(category + canonical_name + missing_in) rather than by DB id, because gap ids are
assigned at seed-import time and are not stable across a fresh data/app.db.
The spread deliberately covers both categories x both directions, two medium-severity
cases, and element_style_variables as the structured-object / decomposition-mismatch
class that LEARNINGS iteration 3 identifies as the real source of difficulty.
`pilot: true` marks the three cases used to validate the harness before committing
hours of agent time to the full set.

cases.why: Medium severity, multi-layer: ordering affects type, parser and render order.
Reverse direction (mobile -> web), exercises the other repo's idioms.
Hardest class: medium-severity component, stresses analyst->implementer translation.
Medium severity behavioural flag — changes control flow, not just a value.
Simple boolean — the floor case. If this needs repair rounds, something is wrong.
Structured object vs flattened keys — the decomposition-mismatch class from LEARNINGS.
Component gap likely to need review — records a realistic failure mode.
Reverse-direction component; native-only capability, may be platform_specific.
